newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end higher on fund news.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end higher on fund news.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed sharply higher on Monday, with market confidence rising after the government announced it was freeing two major state funds to invest in stocks, brokers said.
The weighted index ended 59.67 points or 0.91 percent higher at 6,622.61, the market's highest close since October 14.
Turnover was a heavy T$53.47 billion.

The government announced on Friday and Sunday it would allow the T$188 billion labour insurance fund and the T$24 billion employee pension fund to invest up to 30 percent of their values in the stock market. They had been barred from stock holdings.
The market, mired in a slump for most of October, has gained nearly 300 points in the past four sessions.

"The government's liberalisation measures show it is determined not to let the index continue to fall, and investors are encouraged by that," said Chen Han-chung, securities analyst for Yungli Securities.
Blue-chip electronic shares, boosted by sound earning reports for the first three quarters, led the gains.
High-tech firms were the session's four most heavily traded shares -- with Macronix gaining T$0.90 to T$38.20 and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co rising T$2.50 to T$57.50.
China Steel, Taiwan's biggest steel maker, gained T$0.40 to close at T$25.60.
Brokers expected the market to take a short breather before challenging the 1996 closing high of 6,644.66.
"Share prices already are at a pretty high level and it will not be surprising for profit-taking to emerge tomorrow (Tuesday)," Chen said.
A 6,560-6,650 range was seen for Tuesday.
